title: Onramp Adapter & Telemetry Playbook (draft)
content:
Purpose:
This doc is a low-friction, tactile playbook for building an SDK adapter or "onramp" that gets a Redwood customer from zero to a minimal instrumented integration in ~10-15 minutes. Focus is on a tiny starter kit plus pragmatic telemetry and failure-mode guidance so first-time integrators have clear observability and safe fallbacks.

Audience:
- Platform engineers and SDK owners at customer orgs
- Internal solutions engineers and SDK team members who ship quick integrations

Principles:
- Minimal working surface: make the first successful call obvious and short.
- Instrument by default: include a minimal telemetry bundle so we can surface errors and latencies without heavy config.
- Safe defaults: timeouts, retries, and graceful fallback to a cheaper/compatible model by config.
- Copyable examples: every snippet should be paste-ready.

What this repo/starter includes (minimum viable):
1) adapter-stub/ (single-file adapter for a toy app) - README with 3 commands to run
2) quickstart.md - 3-min quickstart flow for devs
3) telemetry-config.json.example - minimal telemetry hooks (trace_id, sdk_version, route, model_variant)
4) smoke-tests/ - curl + python smoke test scripts
5) examples/python/ and examples/node/ - single-file usage examples

3-minute Quickstart (copy/paste)
- prerequisites: python 3.10, curl, REDWOOD_API_KEY in env

1) Install tiny adapter:
   pip install git+https://github.com/redwood/inference-sdk#adapter-stub

2) Run curl smoke test (paste):
   curl -X POST https://api.redwood.example/v1/generate -H \"Authorization: Bearer $REDWOOD_API_KEY\" -H \"Content-Type: application/json\" -d '{"model":"gpt-4-small","input":"hello world"}'

3) Run local python example:
   export REDWOOD_API_KEY=sk_live_xxx
   python examples/python/quick_adapter_example.py

Telemetry: what we collect (minimal set)
- trace_id (UUID) attached to every request
- sdk_name and sdk_version (auto-injected by adapter)
- route_name or integration_point (e.g., "chat_message_send")
- model_variant (string)
- request_latency_ms and response_size_bytes
- response_status: success | model_error | transport_error | fallback_used

How telemetry flows:
- SDK emits a lightweight JSON line to STDOUT in dev mode (easy to capture) and to a configurable HTTP collector in prod.
- Default collector: telemetry.redwood-internal (stubbed) with auth token in env REDWOOD_TELEMETRY_KEY.

Failure modes and recommended handling (starter policies)
- Transport timeout (client-side): default 3s for small requests, 12s for streaming. Retry once with exponential backoff 300ms -> 900ms.
- Model error (500/502/503): mark response_status=model_error, do not retry if it is deterministic (schema error), otherwise retry with fallback model_variant (e.g., gpt-4-small -> gpt-4-mini).
- Rate limit (429): surface Backoff-At header if present, and queue up to 30s before retry; if queue drains >50% of concurrency budget, return fast-fail to caller with guidance.

Integration checklist (for internal SEs to run when helping a customer):
- [ ] Confirm REDWOOD_API_KEY scope (embed vs. generate)
- [ ] Run curl smoke test and capture telemetry lines
- [ ] Validate trace_id propagation end-to-end (customer logs -> Redwood ingestion)
- [ ] Simulate model_error by sending malformed input and verify response_status=model_error in telemetry
- [ ] Install adapter with --dev to see stdout logs, then flip to prod collector and ensure auth works

Sample python snippet (paste-ready)

from time import time
import os, requests, uuid
REDWOOD_URL = os.getenv('REDWOOD_URL', 'https://api.redwood.example/v1')
API_KEY = os.environ['REDWOOD_API_KEY']
trace_id = str(uuid.uuid4())
headers = {'Authorization': f'Bearer {API_KEY}', 'Content-Type': 'application/json', 'X-Trace-Id': trace_id}
payload = {'model': 'gpt-4-small', 'input': 'Summarize: why is observability useful?'}
start = time()
r = requests.post(f"{REDWOOD_URL}/generate", json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=6)
duration_ms = int((time()-start)*1000)
print({ 'trace_id': trace_id, 'status_code': r.status_code, 'latency_ms': duration_ms })

Telemetry privacy note:
- Only non-sensitive metadata should be sent by default (ids, latencies, sizes). Do not send user PII or full user content unless customer explicitly opts into content-level telemetry and signs the data processing addendum.

Docs & onboarding flow (detailed)
1) Quickstart: minimal install + smoke test (3-5m)
2) Guided lab: enable telemetry collector, run a set of 5 scenario tests (10-20m)
3) Integration checklist + SRE handoff (15-30m)
4) Optional: add canary rollout policy sample (we provide route config template)

Open questions / decisions needed:
- Default collector URL and retention policy for customer demo accounts (ask security/compliance) [owner: Samir]
- Recommend default model fallback tiers and mapping (who owns mapping? product or runtime?) [owner: Product]
- Should we include a tiny built-in latency histogram exporter or just timeseries points? (tradeoff: complexity vs. signal)

Notes to self / working items:
- Build tiny Dockerfile for examples so SEs can demo without python env differences (priority low).
- Add CI smoke job that runs examples on each PR (linked: GH #78).
- Move telemetry config to a single source of truth in examples/telemetry.md and reference Confluence page.

Appendix: example telemetry line (dev mode)
{"trace_id":"c1b2e3f4-...","sdk":"py-adapter","version":"0.1.0-dev","route":"chat_send","model":"gpt-4-small","latency_ms":120,"status":"success"}

---
Casual notes: keep this doc intentionally short. This is a living sketch for SEs and SDK folks; we're aiming for predictable first-call magic and basic observability so customers can move from prototype -> pilot with confidence.
